title: [Performance][BugFix] Optimize A5 QSFA and handle trailing invalid sparse indices
body: ### What this PR does / why we need it? This PR optimizes QSFA on Ascend A5 and fixes sparse-index boundary handling. Performance improvements: - Specialize A5 QK dimensions, packed KV strides, and buffer allocation for optional RoPE. - Add INT8 paged sparse KV address preprocessing with odd-K tail handling. - Hoist gather-loop invariants and copy parameters while retaining scalar fallbacks outside the eligible address-preprocessing path. - Avoid the valid-prefix binary search when sparse indices are unpadded. Correctness improvements: - Clip sparse computation to the valid index prefix regardless of whether softmax LSE is requested, excluding trailing `-1` padding. - Handle empty valid-index ranges without performing unnecessary sparse computation. - Clear the assigned query/head output range when all sparse indices are invalid and the output has not already been initialized, preventing uninitialized output values. The public tiling key, public APIs, and A2/A3 kernel dispatch remain unchanged. ### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change? NO. This PR improves QSFA performance on Ascend A5 and fixes output handling for trailing or fully invalid sparse indices. It does not change public APIs or configuration options. ### How was this patch tested? #### Static and repository checks The following checks passed: - `git diff --check HEAD~2..HEAD` - Ruff check and Ruff format - clang-format - codespell - typos - markdownlint - GitHub Actions workflow linting - Filename, package, import, and other applicable local checks The complete `bash format.sh ci` command was also attempted on Windows, but did not finish cleanly because: - Some hooks require `/bin/bash`, which is unavailable to the Windows pre-commit process. - `shellcheck` is not installed. - The local `check-long-functions` and `check-symbolic-meta` hook commands exited with `9009`. These were local environment failures rather than reported formatting errors in the changed C++ files. The required Linux CI checks remain necessary. #### A5 hardware performance validation The performance change was benchmarked on: - Hardware: 8 x Ascend 950DT (A5) - Model: GLM-5.3-Flash - Parallelism: DP8 / TP1 / EP8 - KV cache dtype: FP8 - Benchmark: `vllm bench serve` with random synthetic data - Method: three runs per version and case, using the same workload and random seeds for each A/B pair - Baseline: `20c44932c6c1f2aa8411e4f8b33e11ae6cd1efae` - Patched version: `cb31d5deb0184bd57ef35af3ec081cb0b9757e17` | Case | Baseline QPS | Patched QPS | QPS change | Average TTFT improvement | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 128K input, 64 requests, concurrency 16 | 1.0790 | 1.1717 | +8.59% | +10.93% | | 4K input, concurrency 64 | 7.0768 | 7.4558 | +5.36% | +6.12% | Standalone QSFA benchmarks with identical synthetic inputs, page tables, and sparse indices showed: | QSFA input | Baseline | Patched | Latency reduction | |---|---:|---:|---:| | 128K KV + 16K query chunk | 35.38 ms | 23.26 ms | 34.25% | | 4K KV + 4K query | 8.89 ms | 5.85 ms | 34.23% | | 128K KV + single query | 0.131 ms | 0.106 ms | 19.19% | These benchmarks cover the performance commit `cb31d5de`. They do not constitute a dedicated correctness regression test for the subsequent trailing-invalid-index fix. #### A5 hardware precision validation: gsm8k aime26 ### Checklist #### Testing - [ ] **Boundary / edge-case coverage**: Automated A5 coverage for empty, fully invalid, and trailing-invalid sparse-index ranges remains pending. - [ ] **Regression test**: A regression test for the trailing-invalid-index output issue remains pending. - [ ] **Error / failure path coverage**: Abnormal sparse-index paths have been addressed in code, but dedicated automated coverage remains pending. - [ ] **Meaningful & reliable tests**: No new tests were added; manual performance results and current static checks are reported above. - [ ] **Performance impact**: Real A5 benchmark results are attached above, including the regressed 128K/16-request case; automated performance regression coverage remains pending. - vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/544f182d9f0c9bfe8bd7645525951d5e3692a542
